1  THIS APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:28.03.2013 PASSED IN MVC NO.1980/2011 ON THE FILE OF THE JUDGE AND XXVI ACMM, MACT, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, BENGLAURU,
DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 30.10.2023, COMING ON FOR 'PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT' THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short) by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Bangalore (SSCH-09), in MVC No.1980/2011, dated 28.03.2013, whereby the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 166 of the MV act.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred with the original ranks occupied by them before the Tribunal.

3. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 19.10.2010, at 8:30 a.m., on Sarjapur Road, near Bellandur Gate, Bangalore, the petitioner was travelling in an autorikshaw bearing registration No.KA05 B 9766 and driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and the said vehicle overturned, resulting in the accident.

She suffered the injuries and hence, she filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.
4.

Respondent No.1-owner did not appear before the Court, while respondent No.2-Insurer filed the objection statement and admitted the Policy in respect of auto bearing registration No.KA 05 B 9766 and validity of the insurance as on the date of the accident.

However, the rest of the allegations were denied and it is specifically contended that the autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA 05 B 9766 was not involved in the accident and the appellant in collusion with her husband and police, along with respondent No.1, falsely implicated the said auto and hence, disputed the liability.

5. The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence, has held that the autoriskhaw bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 was not at all involved in the accident and it was falsely planted in the case and dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved by this judgment of dismissal, this appeal came to be filed.
6. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurer.
Perused the records.

7. The learned counsel for appellant would contend that the accident has occurred on 19.10.2010 and claimant was inmate of the auto which was toppled and she was travelling along with two Smt. Sridevi vs Smt. Sabitha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91850314/
2 persons.

It is also contended that she was a tailor by profession and earning Rs.4,000 per month and the husband under the wrong impression, has given wrong information while lodging the complaint and since injured was regularly travelling in the same vehicle, she has given clear picture and hence, he would content that the said aspect is not properly appreciated.
8. He would also contend that the Investigating Officer was examined on behalf of the Insurance Company as RW1 and he supported the case of the claimants.
Alternatively, he would contend that an opportunity be given to the claimants to examine the other inmates of the vehicle to prove the accident.
Hence, he would seek for allowing the appeal by setting aside the impugned order of dismissal.

9. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that the FIR and complaint clearly disclose that the auto bearing No.KA 05 5684 was involved in the accident and same is referred in the sketch as well as panchanama which were drawn as per the statement of eyewitness.

He would contend that subsequently, in order to have a wrongful gain, his auto bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 was got implicated as it was having valid insurance and the vehicle which met with an accident did not possess valid insurance.

He would also contend that the complaint allegations itself disclose that the complaint was lodged after getting detailed information from the claimant herself by her husband and question of subsequently getting different information does not arise at all.

He would also contend that the accident has occurred on 19.10.2010 and suddenly on 26.10.2010, the vehicle bearing KA05 B 9766 was inspected and there is no evidence as to when it was seized and at whose instance it was seized and no supporting documents were produced regarding the involvement of the said vehicle in the accident.
He would also contend that the cross-examination of PW1 discloses that she is not a routine traveller in the said auto itself so as to remember the vehicle number so as to disclose the same.
Hence, he would contend that the Tribunal has appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper prospective and the judgment does not call for any interference.
Hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeal.
10. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, it is an undisputed fact that the claimant did suffer injuries in road traffic accident.
Ex.P1 is a copy of the FIR and complaint which clearly disclose that the claimant was travelling in auto bearing No.KA 02 5684 when the accident took place.
The records further disclose that she was initially shifted to Suvarnamukhi Hospital and then the complainant has lodged a complaint.
Later on, the claimant was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital and then to Victoria Hospital.
The assertions made in the complaint clearly disclose that complainant got information about this accident from his wife on his mobile.
It clearly discloses that he lodged a complaint after getting admitted his wife into hospital and getting information from his wife i.e., the claimant.
In the FIR and complaint, a specific number of the vehicle was referred by complainant, who is the husband of the claimant.
11. But subsequently, his further statement was recorded by the Investigating Officer, wherein the vehicle was changed by incorporating the vehicle bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 in place of KA 02 5684.
Interestingly, the claimant has not got examined her husband to substantiate this contention.

Her husband would have been the best witness in this regard and when he has lodged a complaint on the basis of information provided by his wife, the question of he again consulting his wife does not arise Smt. Sridevi vs Smt. Sabitha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91850314/
3 at all
. Evidence of PW2 is only regarding the production of documents and it would not assist.
12. RW1 is the Investigating Officer and he was examined on behalf of the Insurance Company.
But he denied the fact that Police have received a complaint from Kashipathi and a spot mazar was drawn.
But admittedly, as per Ex.P1 the complaint was lodged by one Kashipathi himself i.e., the husband of the claimant.
But RW1 disputes this aspect.
The claimant is relying on further statement of her husband as per Ex.P2, but Ex.P2 is a 161 Cr.P.C. statement and it has no relevancy unless the person who has given such a statement is examined.
Hence, Ex.P2 does not assist the claimants in any way.
13. Apart from that, Ex.P3 is a copy of the Mahazar and it was drawn as per the spot shown by the eyewitness, Uday Kumar and Ex.P4 is the sketch.
In both these documents, the vehicle number is shown as KA 02 5684.
But subsequently, on the basis of further statement, the vehicle number was changed as KA 05 B 9766.
Much arguments have been advanced regarding Ex.P8, which is the copy of the order sheet and accusation in CC No.1566/2010, wherein the accused Munikrishna pleaded guilty.
But there is no evidence as to why he appeared voluntarily before the criminal court and how pleaded guilty are not at all forthcoming.
14. The claimant and RW1 assert that the driver of KA 02 5684 was one Ashok and he was shifted injured to the hospital and under the misconception, the complaint was lodged against the said vehicle.
But that was not the statement given in the complaint by the complainant i.e., the husband of the claimant.
But he claims that, on the basis of the information provided by his wife, he lodged a complaint.
How this Ashok got information that a vehicle bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 was involved in the accident is not at all forthcoming.
Further, RW1 did not obtain the Insurance Policy of KA 02 5684 which clearly discloses that the said vehicle did not possess valid insurance.

15. Further, according to the claimant she was travelling in the said auto bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 along with her two colleagues, but interestingly, the said colleagues were also not examined in the instant case and no explanation was offered.
They would have been the best witnesses in the given circumstances.

16. All along, it is asserted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the claimant was regularly travelling in the same auto KA 05 B 9766 and she was conversant with the driver and therefore, she could remember the auto number and narrated the same in the hospital.
But his complaint version is entirely different.

Even otherwise, the claimant, who is examined as PW1 in her cross- examination, admitted that she does not know the owner or driver of auto bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 and she has specifically asserted that she was not regularly travelling in the said auto.
Hence, it cannot be believed that she could recollect the auto number in the hospital and her evidence runs contrary to the evidence of the complaint assertions.
Hence, the evidence lead by the claimant does not inspire the confidence of the Court regarding the involvement of auto bearing No.KA 05 B 9766 in the accident.
17. The learned counsel has much harped on Ex.P8, wherein the auto driver Muniratna has pleaded guilty in CC No.1566/2010.

But the Tribunal in this context, by placing reliance on a decision of this Smt. Sridevi vs Smt. Sabitha on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91850314/
4

Court in ILR 2009 KAR 2921 [Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., vs. B.C.Kumar and another] has held that the conviction in a criminal case that too when it is based on pleading guilty is not a relevant factor while dealing MVC matter before the Tribunal and the accident is required to be proved independently.

entities.text: ILR 2009 KAR 2921 [Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., vs. B.C.Kumar and another]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the said principles, Ex.P8 does not have any relevancy.

As observed above, the claimant has neither examined her husband to show that by misconception he has given wrong number while lodging the complaint nor examined the other two colleagues who were also alleged to be travelling in the auto.
18. The Tribunal has appreciated the oral and documentary evidence in proper perspective and on proper appreciation of evidence, dismissed the claim petition.
No illegality or infirmity is found in the judgment of dismissal passed by the Tribunal so as to call for interference by this Court.

Hence,
the appeal being devoid of any merits does not survive for consideration.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal stands dismissed.
Sd/-
